header.title: Distributed, Cloud and Systems Engineering
header.lead: These courses focus on computing systems beyond isolated programming exercises: operating systems, distributed applications, services, cloud environments, integration layers, and deployment-oriented engineering.

data.text: This family groups operating systems, distributed programming, middleware, cloud computing, service engineering, service-oriented architecture, embedded Linux/systems topics, and programming for secure or distributed environments. The common concern is how software interacts with execution environments, machines, networks, services, and infrastructure.

data.text: The course combines architecture-level reasoning with implementation-oriented exercises. Students are encouraged to understand where the boundaries are: between client and server, local and remote, synchronous and asynchronous, component and service, development and deployment.

items: [b]System thinking[/b]: students analyze a software system as a set of interacting parts.
[b]Failure awareness[/b]: examples include network delays, unavailable services, inconsistent state, and security constraints.
[b]Deployment mindset[/b]: implementation choices are connected to scalability, configuration, and operational behavior.
Design applications that communicate across process, machine, or service boundaries.

Integrate services and APIs while considering security and reliability.
Move from code-only thinking to system-level engineering.
